guarantees.claim: sp_in_valid is driven by the concatenation {in_valid}; only bit 0 receives in_valid's value, any remaining bits (if Sp2VWidth>1) are undriven.
sp_out_ready is driven by the concatenation {out_ready}; only bit 0 receives out_ready's value, remaining bits (if Sp2VWidth>1) are undriven.
sp_crypt is driven by {crypt}, similarly connecting only the least significant bit.

assumptions.claim: The Sparsified FSM width parameter Sp2VWidth must be exactly 1; otherwise, the `assign sp_* = {original}` pattern drives only bit 0, leaving higher bits disconnected.
assumptions.cond: always, when sparsified signals are used by receiver blocks
assumptions.risk: If Sp2VWidth > 1, the redundant copies expected for security/fault detection remain unconnected, potentially causing X propagation, loss of spatial redundancy, and missed errors in secret/key/manipulation paths.

uncertain_points.claim: The Sp2VWidth parameter might be >1 for spatial redundancy, but the conversion assigns ({signal}) only connects one bit. If Sp2VWidth>1, the higher-order bits of sp_* signals are undriven, defeating sparsified redundancy.
uncertain_points.cond: Sp2VWidth > 1 (value not visible in this chunk)
uncertain_points.risk: Loss of multi-rail security protection; undriven bits can lead to metastability, X-propagation into key/cipher FSM, or masked faults bypassing alert mechanisms.

uncertain_points.claim: All top-level outputs (in_ready_o, out_valid_o, crypt_o, dec_key_gen_o, prng_reseed_o, key_clear_o, data_out_clear_o, alert_o, prng_update_o, prng_reseed_req_o, state_sel_o, state_we_o, …) and internal registers (crypt_d/q, dec_key_gen_d/q, prng_reseed, key_clear, data_out_clear, rnd_ctr) are not driven in this chunk; their logic resides in other parts of the module.
uncertain_points.cond: always (chunk covers only declarations and sparse-conversion assigns)
uncertain_points.risk: Missing or erroneous implementation in the excluded module segments can leave critical security outputs undriven or stuck at reset, causing protocol deadlock, cipher mis‑operation, or silent data exposure.
